mustFix.title: Signature StarChart is illegible and un-tappable on phones
mustFix.fix: Add a <640px treatment: raise node/axis label fontSize to ~13-14px OR use non-scaling-text/vector-effect so labels survive the ~0.40 viewBox downscale (10px→~4px today); add a transparent padded hit-circle as the first child of EVERY star <g> (e.g. <circle r=22 fill="transparent" pointer-events="all">) for all states, not just current/mastered, so tap targets clear ~44px; consider a taller/narrower viewBox on small screens. Verify effective width against the card's var(--s-4) padding.

mustFix.title: Star-ignition payoff never spotlights the node just earned; pulse jumps to the NEXT node
mustFix.fix: router.push(`/${locale}/map?ignited=${mod.id}`); read the param via useSearchParams in MapView and thread to StarChart. Give the ignited node a one-shot bloom on arrival (reuse IgniteGlyph ring: r:4→15, opacity:0.9→0, fill=freeze + brief held glow) and scroll it into view, while initializing all other stars to their final lit radius immediately (skip the r:0→r redraw) so only that star animates. Honor prefers-reduced-motion (final lit state, no bloom). Do NOT reuse the 'current' pulse — that ring is the next-node affordance. Fix the stale comment citation to Reward.tsx:103-105.

mustFix.title: Mastery reward always declares 'Strong · into L6 (Staff) territory' regardless of level
mustFix.fix: Remove the toBand/BAND_RANGE placement from the mastery readout — since mastery requires ratio>=0.8 and CUT_STRONG=0.7, it is mathematically always 'strong'/'L6'. Phrase the toast module-locally: en `You mastered ${title}. Module charted on ${axis.name.en}.` / es `Dominaste ${title}. Módulo trazado en ${axis.name.es}.` Reserve axis-level band placement for the diagnostic surfaces (MeView/ResultsView), the only ones entitled to make a composite-score claim.

mustFix.title: Mastery short-circuits the loop — strongest learners never reach Room/Field Work
mustFix.fix: On newlyMastered, keep fireReward but replace `router.push(`/${locale}/map`); return;` with `onDone(); return;` so mastered learners flow through the same read→retrieval→room→field chain as everyone else. Surface the star-chart payoff after Field Work or via an explicit action / the existing '← map' link, not as an automatic eject only the strongest hit.

mustFix.title: Gauntlet line 13 mislabeled 'excessive-agency' (LLM06) — it is prompt injection (LLM01)
mustFix.fix: Reclassify line 13's flaw from 'excessive-agency' to 'injection' (LLM01) — the snippet's model call (lines 32-37) has no tools array, so there is no excessive agency; `note` concatenated into the system prompt (line 30) is a direct injection vector. The existing exploit/fix text already describes injection. Correct the exploit's '(line 21)' reference to '(lines 28-30)'. If LLM06 must stay represented, instead add a genuinely tool-bearing side-effecting action and key a new line to it; otherwise leave no unmatched category for the auto-grader. This currently marks a correct staff-level learner wrong on the centerpiece assessment.

mustFix.title: Pervasive dim text fails WCAG AA contrast on the dark canvas
mustFix.fix: Raise --text-3 alpha from 0.45 (~4.1:1) to ~0.55 (~5:1) — clears the 4.5:1 floor without overshooting to ~7:1 and flattening the scale. --text-3 is the .eyebrow instrument voice used app-wide, so this is systemic. Switch any --text-4 (0.28, ~2.3:1) that carries information (StarChart L-band labels L3-L7, Diagram/CodeRedTeam axis+stat labels) to --text-3-or-better. Keep --text-4 only for decorative marks like the page.tsx line numbers.

mustFix.title: Copy says 'five axes' but six axes ship (radar, runner, messages, aria-label)
mustFix.file: src/components/Radar.tsx (54 aria-label + line 1 comment); src/components/AssessRunner.tsx (99); src/lib/messages.ts (27)
mustFix.fix: axes.ts defines six axes (id 6 = Real World AI Engineering) and Radar special-cases a.id===6, drawing six spokes while announcing five. Update all copy to six/seis, and prefer dynamic interpolation from AXES.length (e.g. `across ${n} axes`) in Radar.tsx and AssessRunner.tsx so it can't drift again; for messages.ts (no AXES scope) hardcode 'six/seis' or refactor to build the string where AXES is in scope. Optionally name the AI axis in the radar aria-label for the flagship vertex. Fix the stale '5-axis' comment at Radar.tsx line 1.

mustFix.title: 'You are here' altitude horizon is frozen — all 14 modules are L5, so it never climbs
mustFix.fix: altitudeY snaps to 0.54 on first mastery and never moves (horizon always reads 'YOU ARE HERE · L5'), and the marker doesn't exist before first mastery. Re-base altitude on within-band progress: interpolate toward the next band by (mastered in band / total in band) as a rising fill/line that appears at the band floor even at zero mastery. Track-color the horizon by the axis/track of the node that set the current altitude — replace hardcoded var(--gen)/var(--gen-accent) at 145-147,158 with accent(track) passed up from MapView. (Authoring L4/L6 modules is the real long-term fix.)

mustFix.title: 0.8 CBM mastery gate penalizes honest correct-but-unconfident answers
mustFix.fix: Verified: all-correct/low-confidence = 0.778 (mastery DENIED), so passing effectively requires marking 'high' — teaching confidence inflation; and 4-high-correct+1-high-wrong = exactly 0.80 (passes), so a confident-wrong doesn't reliably block. Decouple the gate: require correctness ratio >= 0.8 AND a separate calibration check, so a fully-correct hedger unlocks while a confident-wrong measurably drops the calibration component; or apply the §B4 confident-wrong cap (currently only in scoreAxis) to the module gate. Correct the store.ts:73-75 comment: mid-confidence, not only high, already clears the gate. (Medium confidence — real per the numbers, but the exact remedy is a design choice; rank last of the must-fixes.)

shouldFix.title: Break the antithesis 'X is a Y, not a Z' title formula (8 of 30 titles)
shouldFix.file: AI-L5 module titles + general-l5 track (JSON content)
shouldFix.fix: Keep the 'not X' reversal at most 2-3 times where reframing the misconception IS the lesson (e.g. OWASP 'threat model, not a compliance checklist'). Convert the rest to flat imperatives/noun phrases: 'Chunking is a modeling decision, not a preprocessing step'→'Chunk to preserve a unit of meaning'; 'The tool description is a prompt, not documentation'→'Write the tool description as a prompt'; 'Agent memory is an architecture, not a bigger context window'→'Agent memory is an architecture problem'. Note the 'Autonomy is a spectrum…' sub-lesson duplicates the module title at L1869. Apply to general-l5 parallels too.

shouldFix.title: Landing + gauntlet reuse one verbatim 'the A, the B, the p99 cliff, the Z' list three times
shouldFix.fix: Keep the landing hero sub (page.tsx:14) as canonical; rewrite gauntletDesc (page.tsx:43) so the same page doesn't repeat 'p99 cliff' or the dash-list cadence, and reword gauntlet.ts:68 so the brief doesn't mirror the landing verbatim. Apply to both en and es strings.

shouldFix.title: 'Lethal trifecta' invoked but the snippet has no exfiltration channel
shouldFix.fix: Reframe the n:13 exploit only: the tool-less model gives untrusted input + private data but NO external channel, so it is explicitly NOT the lethal trifecta — and staying tool-less is how you avoid it. State the real blast radius (injection poisons the summary → unparameterized INSERT at n:43 → returned to internal agent). Leave n:28 (indirect injection) essentially as-is; at most note the 'email' payload is illustrative of what this model can't execute.

shouldFix.title: will-change left permanently on every revealed element
shouldFix.fix: Add `will-change: auto;` to the revealed selector at globals.css:404 so `[data-reveal][data-armed="true"][data-revealed="true"]` drops the compositor layer after the one-shot reveal. The CSS override alone resolves it; a transitionend cleanup is optional.

shouldFix.title: Mobile nav sheet lacks Escape-to-close, focus management, and adequate tap targets
shouldFix.fix: Give the sheet id="nav-sheet" and aria-controls on the burger; add a keydown handler that closes on Escape and returns focus to the burger (via ref); move focus to the first sheet link on open. Bump burger padding and the language link (currently 12px .eyebrow, 3px 8px padding) to clear at least 24px (WCAG 2.5.8) and ideally 44px. Focus-trap optional (disclosure, not modal).

shouldFix.title: StarChart keyboard focus has no reliable visible indicator
shouldFix.fix: The global :focus-visible outline on SVG <g> is unreliable in Safari/Firefox. Track a dedicated focusedId (from existing onFocus/onBlur) and render an explicit ring for that node inside the SVG: <circle r={r+4} fill="none" stroke="var(--ai-signal)" strokeWidth={2}> when n.id===focusedId. Optionally suppress the loose global outline on these <g> nodes.

shouldFix.title: Film-grain overlay sits above all UI with a fixed full-viewport blend mode
shouldFix.fix: Lower body::before z-index from 9999 to just above content but below interactive/overlay UI (e.g. 1), or scope it to a background element so it never composites over focus rings or the reward toast (z 200). If scroll/INP still regresses from the fixed mix-blend-mode:overlay, swap to a plain low-opacity texture (or soft-light/multiply) on a non-fixed isolated element.

shouldFix.title: Signal is a meaningless bare integer — the one XP-cosplay crack in the prestige aesthetic
shouldFix.fix: Signal is incremented by fixed 20/15/40 and never spent, ranked, or mapped — 'Signal: 75' and '+40 SIGNAL' read as XP. Best: replace the bare count on MeView.tsx:35 with a derived named readout from the existing responseLog/moduleScores (e.g. a per-axis calibration index or 'reading L5 across N axes'). If out of scope, delete the Signal tile and the '+N SIGNAL' block (keep the informational toast title/body) and fix the '"XP"' comment at store.ts:17.

shouldFix.title: Cadence is dead code and there is no return hook
shouldFix.fix: cadence.enabled gates nothing and weeks[] is never written/read; as a localStorage-only static export there's no channel to deliver the promised weekly rhythm. Either (A) remove the Cadence card + store field until a backend/email seam exists, or (B) add lastMasteredAt: Record<string,number> written in masterModule, compute a spaced-repetition 'due for review' set, and surface it on Me/Map when cadence.enabled — the only viable localStorage return hook. Drop the unused weeks[] either way.

shouldFix.title: Gauntlet boss has zero replay value and gates nothing
shouldFix.fix: The debrief reveals every planted flaw with line numbers, so 'Run it again' is a trivial memorized 100% and bestScore becomes noise. (1) Track and surface FIRST-attempt (cold-read) score instead of bestScore — the only unbiased signal of the 30%-judgment skill. (2) Render GAUNTLET_NODE with state 'mastered' when clearedAt is set so the win shows on the chart. Optionally rotate 2-3 flaw subsets, or don't re-show the annotated debrief on retry.

verdict: HOLD FOR POLISH PASS — not yet ready to submit as award-worthy, but genuinely close and genuinely not AI-slop. Across all five dimensions the underlying craft is real and above the bar for authenticity: the copy is opinionated and technically current, the module bodies are technically impeccable for late-2025/2026, the design is a coherent instrument system with disciplined motion and authored SVG, and the Gauntlet is a novel non-fakeable assessment format. Honest per-dimension: Originality 7, Design 7, Technical 7, Pedagogy 6, Gamification 7. What holds it back is a tight cluster of centerpiece defects, not a rewrite: the signature StarChart is illegible/un-tappable on phones (the most common device), the named 'watch your node light up' payoff actually spotlights the wrong node, the mastery reward lies to every learner ('Strong · into L6' always), the advertised read→check→Room→boss loop ejects the strongest learners early, the centerpiece Gauntlet marks a correct staff answer wrong on an OWASP mislabel, dim instrument text fails WCAG AA app-wide, and the product contradicts itself on 'five vs six axes.' These are catchable in minutes by exactly the skeptical senior/jury this targets, and every one is a scoped fix. Land the nine must-fixes (plus the anti-slop rhythm-breaking should-fixes, which are the true 'not-AI-generated' deductions) and this clears the hard bar. Ranking of must-fixes is by hard-bar impact: visible centerpiece breakage and false/contradictory statements first, systemic-but-quieter accessibility and the honesty-gate design question last.
